data.gender_notes: Saburah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Saburah is derived from the Arabic word 'saburah' which means patience and endurance. It is a beautiful name for a baby girl that signifies strength and resilience in the face of adversity. The name Saburah carries the meaning “Patience, Endurance” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Saburah usually hope their child will grow to embody patience, endurance and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Saburah holds deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture. It is believed that the name embodies the qualities of Sabur, the name of Allah that signifies patience and forbearance. A child named Saburah is believed to be blessed with these qualities and will grow up to be a strong and resilient individual who can weather any storm in life.
data.etymology: Saburah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Patience, Endurance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saburah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

In the Islamic tradition, patience is considered one of the most important qualities that a believer should possess. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said, "Patience is a light which Allah puts in the heart of Believers." (Bukhari and Muslim)

(21:107) Saburah is a name that inspires its bearer to strive to embody the mercy and compassion of Allah towards herself and others.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (The Beginning and The End) - Volume 10, page 338 The name Saburah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: 632 AD - 661 AD (11 years after Prophet Muhammad's death)
historical_references.context: Aisha bint Abu Bakr, the wife of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), made a vow to perform a pilgrimage to Mecca and to visit the grave of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) every year if she was granted the opportunity to live. Aisha named her servant girl, Saburah, who was with her on her journey, as her heir and executor of her will. Aisha instructed Saburah to perform a pilgrimage on her behalf every year and to visit the Prophet's grave and offer prayers for her.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hadid's Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah - Volume 1, page 112 The name Saburah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Saburah is mentioned in a hadith narrated by Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) regarding serving the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his household. Saburah was a servant of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (pbuh), who was known for her generosity. One day, a poor man came to Aisha and asked for food. Aisha asked Saburah to feed him, but Saburah replied that she had already given away all the food she had. The Prophet (pbuh) overheard their conversation and instructed Saburah to prepare food for the man from his own portion of the meal. The Prophet (pbuh) then said, 'Whoever helps a believing man or woman, it is as if he has helped me.' (Sahih Muslim)
